questions.q: Let $\alpha = \mathop\max_{x \in \mathbb{R}}\left\{{8}^{2\sin 3x} \cdot {4}^{4\cos 3x}\right\}$ and~$\beta = \mathop\min_{x \in \mathbb{R}}\left\{{8}^{2\sin 3x} \cdot {4}^{4\cos 3x}\right\} .$ If $8x^{2} + bx + c = 0$~is a quadratic equation whose roots are ${α}^{1 / 5}$ and ${β}^{1 / 5},$~then the value of $c - b$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\alpha = max\left\{{8}^{2\sin 3x} \cdot {4}^{4\cos 3x}\right\}$

$= max\left\{{2}^{6\sin 3x} \cdot {2}^{8\cos 3x}\right\}$

$= max\left\{{2}^{6\sin 3x + 8\cos 3x}\right\}$

and $\beta = min\left\{{8}^{2\sin 3x} \cdot {4}^{4\cos 3x}\right\} = min\left\{{2}^{6\sin 3x + 8\cos 3x}\right\}$

Now range of $6\sin 3x + 8\cos 3x$

$= \left[- $\sqrt{{6}^{2} + {8}^{2}}, + \sqrt{{6}^{2} + {8}^{2}}\right] = \left[-$10, 10\right]$

$\alpha = {2}^{10}& \beta = {2}^{- 10}$

So, ${α}^{1 / 5} = {2}^{2} = 4$

$⇒ {β}^{1 / 5} = {2}^{- 2} = $\dfrac{1}{4}

The quadratic $8x^{2} + bx + c = 0,$

sum of roots~=\dfrac{- b}{8}~and product of roots~=\dfrac{c}{8}

$∴ c - b = 8 \times [ ($product of roots$) + ($sum of roots$) ]$

$= 8 \times \left[4 \times $\dfrac{1}{4} +$4 + $\dfrac{1}{4}\right] =$8 \times \left[\dfrac{21}{4}\right] =42

$

questions.solution:
$∵$ Quadratic expression is positive, hence $1 + 2m > 0$ and $D < 0$

$⇒ m > \dfrac{- 1}{2}$ and

$4{\left(1 + 3m\right)}^{2} - 16\left(1 + m\right)\left(1 + 2m\right) < 0$

$⇒ 9m^{2} + 1 + 6m - 4 \left($2m^{2} + 3m + 1\right) < 0$

$⇒ m^{2} - 6m - 3 < 0$

$⇒ \left(m - 3 + 2\sqrt{3}\right) \left(m - 3 - 2\sqrt{3}\right)< 0$

$⇒ m \in \left($3 - $2\sqrt{3},$3 + $2\sqrt{3}\right)

$∴ m = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$

questions.q: The minimum value of the sum of the squares of the roots of& $x^{2} + \left(3 - a\right)x = 2a - 1$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation

$x^{2} + \left(3 - a\right)x + 1 - 2a = 0$

Then, sum of roots~$\alpha + \beta = a - 3$

And product of roots~$\alpha\beta = 1 - 2a$

We know that~${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = \left(\alpha + \beta\right)2 - 2\alpha\beta$

$∴ {α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = \left(a - 3\right)2 - 2 \left($1 - 2a\right)$

$= a^{2} - 2a + 7$

$= \left($a - 1\right)2 + 6$

$∴$ Minimum value of ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = 6$~at~$a = 1.

$

questions.q: The equation $e^{4x} + 8e^{3x} + 13e^{2x} - 8e^{x} + 1 = 0, x \in R$ has :
options: four solutions two of which are negative
two solutions and both are negative
two solutions and only one of them is negative
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$e^{4x} + 8e^{3x} + 13e^{2x} - 8e^{x} + 1 = 0, x \in R$

Now let $e^{x} = t$~we get,

$t^{4} + 8t^{3} + 13t^{2} - 8t + 1 = 0$

Now divide complete equation by $t^{2}$

$⇒ t^{2} + \dfrac{1}{t2} + 8\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + 13 = 0$

$⇒ \left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2 + 8\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + 15 = 0$

Now let~$t - \dfrac{1}{t} = z$~we get,

$⇒ z^{2} + 8z + 15 = 0$

$⇒ z = - 3, - 5$

So,~$t - \dfrac{1}{t} = - 3$~ or $t - \dfrac{1}{t} = - 5$

$⇒ t^{2} + 3t - 1 = 0$~ or $t^{2} + 5t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{- 3 \pm \sqrt{13}}{2}, \dfrac{- 5 \pm \sqrt{29}}{2}$

So,~$e^{x} = \dfrac{- 3 + \sqrt{13}}{2}, \dfrac{- 5 + \sqrt{29}}{2} = \alpha, \beta$~(rejecting negative values as exponential is positive function)

And both $\dfrac{- 3 + \sqrt{13}}{2}$ and $\dfrac{- 5 + \sqrt{29}}{2} \in \left(0, 1\right)$

So,~$x = \ln \left(\alpha\right),\ln \left(\beta\right)& are& both negative,

Hence, there are two solution and both are negative.

$

questions.q: Let $\lambda \ne 0$ be in $R$. If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation, $x^{2} - x + 2\lambda = 0$ and $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ are the roots of the equation, $3x^{2} - 10x + 27\lambda = 0,$ then $\dfrac{\beta\gamma}{λ}$ is equal to:

questions.solution:
Satisfying& $\alpha$~we have,

$3{α}^{2} - 10\alpha + 27\lambda = 0 \ldots \left(i\right)$~and
$3{α}^{2} - 3\alpha +6\lambda = 0 \ldots \left(ii\right)$
Subtract

$- 7\alpha +21\lambda = 0$
$3\lambda = \alpha$
by \left(ii\right)$, $9{λ}^{2} - 3\lambda + 2\lambda = 0$
$⇒ \lambda = 0, \dfrac{1}{9}\text{but}\lambda \ne0$
$∴$~Given equation are $x^{2} - x + \dfrac{2}{9} =0$ and $3x^{2} - 10x + 3 = 0$
$∴ \alpha = \dfrac{1}{3}, \beta = \dfrac{2}{3}, \alpha = \dfrac{1}{3}, \gamma =3$
$∴ \dfrac{\beta\gamma}{λ} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot 3}{19} =18$

$

questions.q: Let& $f  \left(x\right)$ be a quadratic polynomial such that~$f\left(– 1\right) + f\left(2\right) = 0$. If one of the roots of~$f\left(x\right) = 0$ is $3, then its other root lies in$

questions.solution:
Let $f\left(x\right) = ax^{2} + bx + c$~be a quadratic equation with roots~$\alpha, \beta$

$f\left(2\right) + f\left(- 1\right) = 0 ⇒ 5a + b + 2c = 0$

~Also~$f\left(3\right) = 0 ⇒ 9a + 3b + c = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{- 5} = \dfrac{b}{13} = \dfrac{c}{6}$

Product of roots~$\alpha\beta = \dfrac{c}{a} = - \dfrac{6}{5}$

We know~$\alpha = 3 ⇒ \beta = - \dfrac{2}{5} \in \left(-1, 0\right)

$

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the distinct roots of the equation $x^2-\left(t^2-5 t+6\right) x+1=0, t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n$. Then the minimum value of $\frac{a_{2023}+a_{2025}}{a_{2024}}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
by newton's theorem
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}+2}-\left(\mathrm{t}^2-5 \mathrm{t}+6\right) \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}+1}+\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}=0 \\
& \therefore \mathrm{a}_{2025}+\mathrm{a}_{2023}=\left(\mathrm{t}^2-5 \mathrm{t}+6\right) \mathrm{a}_{2024} \\
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{a}_{2025}+\mathrm{a}_{2023}}{\mathrm{a}_{2024}}=\mathrm{t}^2-5 \mathrm{t}+6 \\
& \because \mathrm{t}^2-5 \mathrm{t}+6=\left(\mathrm{t}-\frac{5}{2}\right)^2-\frac{1}{4} \\
& \therefore \text { minimum value }=-\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let& $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$~be the three~ roots of the equation~$x^{3} + bx + c = 0$~if~$\beta\gamma = 1 = - \alpha$~then~$b^{3} + 2c^{3} - 3{α}^{3} - 6{β}^{3} - 8{γ}^{3}$& is equal to&
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that roots of& $x^{3} + bx + c = 0$~are~$\alpha, \beta, \gamma$

Also given that

$\beta\gamma = 1 = - \alpha$

$⇒ \alpha = - 1 . . . ( i )$

Now let us apply the relation between the roots of the cubic equation with the coefficients.

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 0 . . . ( ii )$

$⇒ \alpha\beta\gamma = - c . . . ( iii )$

$⇒ \left(- 1\right)\left(1\right) = - c$

$∴ c = 1 . . . ( iv )$

On substituting the value of~$\alpha = - 1$~in eq~ \left(ii\right)$~we get,

$\beta + \gamma = 1 . . . ( v )$

$∵ \alpha\beta + \beta\gamma + \gamma\alpha = b$

$⇒ \alpha\left(\beta + \gamma\right) + \beta\gamma = b$

$∴ b = 0 . . . ( vi )$

Hence, equation will be,

$x^{3} + 1 = 0$

Whose roots will be,~$- 1, - \omega, - {ω}^{2}$

We know that~$1 + \omega + {ω}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta + \gamma = 0$

$⇒ - 1 + \beta + \gamma = 0$

$∴ \beta = - \omega, \gamma = - {ω}^{2} . . . ( vii )$

$⇒ {β}^{3} = - {ω}^{3} = - 1$~and~$⇒ {γ}^{3} = - {ω}^{6} = - 1$

Hence the value of~

$b^{3} + 2c^{3} - 3{α}^{3} - 6{β}^{3} - 8{γ}^{3}$~is

$= 0 + 2 + 3 + 6 + 8$

$= 19$

Hence this is the correct option.

$

We have,& $x^{2} + ( 3 - \lambda ) x + 2 = \lambda, \text{have roots}\alpha \text{ and } \beta .$

$f^{′}\left(\lambda\right) = 2\lambda - 4 = 0{ for~the minimum value of f\left(\lambda\right) }$$

As~$f^{''} ( \lambda ) = 2 > 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 2

questions.q: Let $a, b \in R$~be such that the equation $ax^{2} - 2bx + 15 = 0$~has repeated root $\alpha$~and if $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $x^{2} - 2bx + 21 = 0$,~then ${α}^{2} + {β}^{2}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $ax^{2} - 2bx + 15 = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$~

Has repeated~roots~So~$D = 0$

$4b^{2} - 4 \times15 \timesa = 0$~

$⇒$~$b^{2} = 15a . . . \left(ii\right)$

Also given~

Now~$\alpha$~will satisfy both quadratic

$ax^{2} - 2bx + 15 = 0 \text{ and } x^{2} - 2bx + 21 = 0$

Putting the value we get

$a{α}^{2} - 2b\alpha +15 = 0{α}^{2} - 2b\alpha +21 = 0 - + - - - - - - - - - - - \left(a - 1\right){α}^{2} = 6$

${α}^{2} = \dfrac{6}{a - 1}$

Now in equation (1) product of Root ${α}^{2} = \dfrac{15}{a}$

So~$\dfrac{15}{a} = \dfrac{6}{a - 1}⇒ 2a = 5a - 5 ⇒ a = \dfrac{5}{3}$

Now~$b^{2} = 15a ⇒ b^{2} = 15 \times \dfrac{5}{3}$~$⇒ b^{2} = 25$

So~$b = \pm5$

Now in quadratic $x^{2} - 2bx + 21 = 0$~

Putting the value of~$b$~we get

$x^{2} - 10x + 21 = 0⇒ \left(x - 7\right)\left(x - 3\right) = 0$

So~$x = 3$~or $7$.

Or~

$x^{2} + 10x + 21 = 0 ⇒ x = - 3orx = - 7$

So ~$\alpha = \pm3 \text{ and } \beta = \pm7$

So~${α}^{2} + {β}^{2} = {3}^{2} + {7}^{2} = 9 + 49 = 58$

questions.q: If three distinct numbers $a, b, c$ are in G.P. and the equations $ax^{2} + 2bx + c = 0$ and $dx^{2} + 2ex + f = 0$ have a common root, then which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∵ a, b, c$ are in G.P. $⇒ b^{2} = ac\ldots ( i )$
Equation $ax^{2} + 2bx + c = 0$
Hence, $D = 4b^{2} - 4ac = 0 \left(∵ b^{2} = ac\right)$
$⇒$ equation has equal roots $⇒$ roots are =\dfrac{- b}{a}, \dfrac{- b}{a} ($∵$ sum of roots $\alpha + \alpha = $\dfrac{- 2b}{a} )
$∵$~Both equations have one root in common.
$∴$~Common root is $- $\dfrac{b}{a}.~It will satisfy equation.
$∴ $d{ \left(\dfrac{- b}{a}\right)}^{2} + $2e\left(-$b\right)a + f = 0 ⇒ db^{2} - 2aeb + a^{2}f = 0$
$⇒ d \left($ac\right) - 2aeb + a^{2}f = 0 \left($∵ b^{2} = ac\right)$
$⇒ dc - 2aeb + af = 0$
$⇒ $\dfrac{dc}{ac} - \dfrac{2eb}{ac} + \dfrac{af}{ac} =$0$ (dividing by $ac$ )
$⇒ $\dfrac{d}{a} - \dfrac{2eb}{b^{2}} + \dfrac{f}{c} = -$⇒ $\dfrac{d}{a} + \dfrac{f}{c} = \dfrac{2e}{b}
$⇒ $\dfrac{d}{a}, \dfrac{e}{b}, \dfrac{f}{c}are in A.P.$

questions.q: The sum of all real roots of equation& \left(e^{2x} - 4\right)\left(6e^{2x} - 5e^{x} + 1\right) = 0$ \text{ and } is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $e^{x} = t$~ so,~$e^{2x} = t^{2}$

So, the given equation becomes,~\left(t^{2} - 4\right)\left(6t^{2} - 5t + 1\right) = 0$

$t^{2} - 4 = 0$~(or)~$6t^{2} - 5t + 1 = 0$

$t^{2} = 4$~ ~(or)~$6t^{2} - 3t - 2t + 1 = 0$

$t = \pm 2$~(or) $3t\left(2t - 1\right) - 1\left(2t - 1\right) = 0$

$t = \pm 2$~(or) \left(3t - 1\right)\left(2t - 1\right) = 0$

$t = \pm 2$~(or)~$t = \dfrac{1}{3}$~(or)~$t = \dfrac{1}{2}$

But,~$e^{x} = t > 0 \left(∵ e^{x} > 0; \forall x \in R\right)$

$∴$~ Only possible values for~$t$~are~$2, $\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{1}{2}

When~$t = 2, e^{x} = 2 ⇒ x = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(2\right)$~(or)~$\ln 2$

When~$t = \dfrac{1}{3},e^{x} = \dfrac{1}{3}⇒ x = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)~or~$- \ln 3$

When~$t = $\dfrac{1}{2},$e^{x} = $\dfrac{1}{2}$⇒ x = \log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$~or~$- \ln 2$

$∴$~ The sum of roots of given equation~$= \ln 2 - \ln 3 - \ln 2 = - \ln 3$.

$
